items.impact: The registry cannot by itself authorize ordinary product nodes or claim buildability, which prevents storage-contract materialization from being mistaken for runtime readiness.
items.statement: The root contract fixes schema identity and ownership, enumerates launch-critical families, forces the buildability gate to remain false, and forbids ordinary WorkNodes and NodeSeeds in this storage-only scope.
items.title: Root registry enforces a storage-only non-buildability boundary

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Read by exact key during PlanApproved/PlanCompileRun recovery; stale hashes block launch and route back to Planning Wizard refresh.",

items.impact: Exact-key replay and stale-hash refusal provide a clear safety oracle for ApprovedPlanPack recovery and preserve lineage across version changes.
items.statement: ApprovedPlanPack is a closed canonical MessagePack value with identity, source and policy hashes, lineage retention, ref-only sensitive bodies, and a fail-closed stale-hash replay rule; the approval outbox separately defines idempotent publication states.
items.title: Approved plan and approval outbox contracts are explicitly replay-bound

items.impact: Schemas can accept a pack with no source refs and outbox rows whose status conflicts with publication ids, retry count, or error ref, weakening replay, redaction auditability, and deterministic recovery.
items.statement: Required ref arrays have no non-empty or uniqueness constraints, hash fields are only non-empty strings, and the outbox schema has no conditional invariants tying pending, published, acked, or failed status to publication ids, retry_count, and last_error_ref.
items.title: Pack evidence and outbox state are structurally valid even when semantically contradictory

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.impact: Resume is fail-closed and cannot silently convert bootstrap design state into executable product work.
items.statement: PlanCompileRun explicitly restricts launch source, contract mode and runtime adapter, and stale currentness, unsupported mode, or missing receipts keep compilation disabled.
items.title: PlanCompile bootstrap replay is explicitly runtime-disabled

items.impact: Arbitrary or empty cursor, currentness, cancellation, supersession, source-hash and policy objects can pass validation, so resume, cancellation and stale-state decisions lack a falsifiable stored contract.
items.statement: PlanCompileRun's operationally decisive nested objects are declared only as object, with no properties, required keys, additional-property policy, or status-dependent relationships.
items.title: PlanCompile resume and lifecycle state are opaque to the schema

items.impact: A wave can validate with empty or overlapping read, write, forbidden and parent-only sets, or report completion without a completion receipt, allowing conflicting writes and unverifiable parent writeback.
items.statement: CompilerWaveContract names read/write/forbidden/parent-only boundaries and receipt fields but does not enforce non-empty sets, uniqueness, disjointness, path shape, or result_status relationships to completion_receipt and parent_writeback_required.
items.title: Compiler wave isolation is prose-only at validation time

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay restores graph draft revisions for inspection and validation only; activation stays blocked until PNC-019.",

items.impact: Stored graph revisions remain inspectable without being misrepresented as an executable WorkGraph.
items.statement: WorkGraphDraft is explicitly historical validation state rather than activation authority, and WorkNodeRequest is explicitly not a WorkNode, NodeSeed, candidate queue, or executable task.
items.title: Draft graph and node request values preserve non-executable GUI truth

items.impact: Empty graphs, duplicate nodes, dangling entrypoints or edges, cycles, contradictory authority and fabricated integrity or validation objects all satisfy the value schema; no graph-size limit is expressed.
items.statement: WorkGraphDraft models nodes and dependency edges as unconstrained objects and graph_integrity, scheduler_policy, authority and validation_state as opaque objects, with no referential, acyclicity, non-empty or scale constraints.
items.title: WorkGraphDraft does not validate graph semantics

items.impact: Executor intake can receive a formally valid request with no source PlanUnits, surfaces, acceptance criteria, validators, capabilities or dependencies and with arbitrary test, routing, ordering, authority and cancellation objects.
items.statement: WorkNodeRequest requires the right field names and GUI booleans but its arrays need not be non-empty or unique and its operational objects have no internal schema, leaving acceptance, authority, routing, accessibility-relevant GUI work and cancellation semantics to builders.
items.title: WorkNodeRequest can be complete in shape but empty in executable meaning

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay uses the report to explain accepted/rejected/blocked intake without launching activation when runtime is disabled.",

items.impact: Consumers can explain intake outcomes and receipt history without converting a projection or summary into activation proof.
items.statement: ExecutorIntakeReport and AttemptReceipt name producers and GUI/certification/audit consumers, preserve replay evidence, and explicitly deny activation authority to report or receipt summaries while runtime remains disabled.
items.title: Executor intake and attempt receipts are explanatory, not activation authority

items.impact: An accepted intake may carry empty or failing domain-result objects, rejected or blocked rows may omit their reason codes, and acceptance timestamps or execution context refs can contradict status.
items.statement: All seven intake preflight result fields are unconstrained objects and the schema has no conditional relationship between intake_status, domain outcomes, reason codes, accepted_at_utc and execution_unit_context_ref.
items.title: Executor intake acceptance has no schema-enforced oracle

items.impact: Completed receipts can lack validators or evidence, failed receipts can have meaningless retry or rollback routes, and cancellation or supersession carries no status-specific evidence requirement.
items.statement: AttemptReceipt closes the outer object but leaves result_summary opaque, receipt_kind free-form, all artifact/evidence/validator arrays optionally empty, and status unrelated to retry_route, rollback_route, safe point or unresolved risks.
items.title: Attempt receipts do not prove their outcome or recovery route

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Index row points back to authoritative seglog bytes and is rebuildable; replay ordering uses segment generation, segment order, offset, and sequence_id.",

items.impact: The index remains disposable and replay authority stays with retained seglog bytes, preventing index projections from becoming accidental event canon.
items.statement: EventRecordIndex explicitly binds lookup rows to authoritative seglog bytes and replay ordering, while BlockedProjection is rebuildable from events and receipts and must fail closed when stale or degraded.
items.title: Index and blocked projections preserve source-event authority

items.impact: Malformed hashes and unconstrained segment or event identifiers can pass validation, reducing corruption detection and allowing replay lookup failures to surface only at runtime.
items.statement: EventRecordIndex requires payload_sha256 but constrains it only to a non-empty string; reference and identifier formats likewise lack canonical patterns, and nullable causation_event_id can be an empty string.
items.title: Event index integrity fields lack canonical validation

items.impact: A stale, rebuilding, degraded or unavailable projection may still carry allowed mutation actions and empty source provenance, letting a GUI present unsafe actions despite the prose fail-closed rule.
items.statement: BlockedProjection enumerates freshness and health independently but does not constrain valid pairs, require source_event_ids, order timestamps, or force allowed_action_ids empty when freshness or health is unsafe.
items.title: Blocked-projection GUI safety is stated but not schema-enforced

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Goal state replay consumes append-only goal events plus goal receipts; projections are disposable and stale projections cannot certify completion.",

items.impact: Goal completion cannot be certified from stale GUI state, and legacy/deferred rows remain migration lineage rather than launch authority.
items.statement: Goal receipt replay preserves append-only event and receipt authority, explicitly rejects stale projection certification, and states that Tier 0C-2 receipt materialization does not close the Goal Runtime lifecycle blocker.
items.title: Goal receipt authority is separated from projection and lifecycle closure

items.impact: A goal receipt can certify accepted with no validator output, evidence or child/worknode receipt, while still listing unresolved risks; rejected or blocked decisions need no reason evidence.
items.statement: GoalReceipt requires certification-related arrays and a decision enum but permits every array to be empty, leaves receipt_kind and certification_tier free-form, and defines no decision-dependent oracle.
items.title: Goal certification can be accepted without positive evidence

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Migration-read only until a current run-record owner materializes a v1 value schema.",

items.impact: Builders are not invited to infer runtime value shapes for legacy run, node, generic receipt, attempt, concern or execution-unit inventories before their named owners and reopen conditions mature.
items.statement: The later families in this window consistently declare deferred_not_build_blocking status, migration-read or owned-elsewhere behavior, named deferred owners, reasons and reopen conditions rather than pretending their placeholder field lists are implementation schemas.
items.title: Legacy and later family inventories have explicit defer-and-reopen boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal workspace layout and selected ids as historical GUI state only; replay never certifies terminal process liveness.",

items.impact: Restored terminal layout cannot be presented as evidence that a child process is still running, and transcript, environment and credential bodies are excluded from layout rows.
items.statement: The terminal workspace, section, tab, pane, leaf and workgroup families consistently describe persisted values as historical GUI layout and ref-only metadata, with runtime liveness requiring separate revalidation.
items.title: Terminal layout replay is correctly separated from process liveness

items.impact: Schemas accept split panes with no children or axis, leaf panes with children, duplicate or cyclic child links, multiple roots and negative or oversized fractions, so restored layouts can be corrupt or pathological.
items.statement: TerminalPaneRecord enumerates split versus leaf but does not condition parent, children, split_axis or size_fraction on pane kind, bound fractions, require unique children, prevent self-links/cycles, or cap tree breadth and depth.
items.title: Terminal pane trees are not structurally validated

items.impact: Empty, duplicate or dangling order entries and active ids can restore inconsistent selections; empty titles and unconstrained display strings leave localization and accessible naming behavior unspecified.
items.statement: Workspace, section and workgroup order arrays lack minItems, uniqueness and referential constraints; active ids need not occur in their order arrays, and visible titles permit empty strings with no localization or accessibility contract.
items.title: Terminal grouping and selection state can restore dangling GUI references

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores historical session identity and status; active process identity must be revalidated by runtime before reuse.",
"replay_behavior": "Restores command history by scrubbed refs only; command blocks are historical evidence and not runtime authority.",

items.impact: Historical sessions and command blocks cannot silently regain process authority, and secret-bearing command or transcript bodies remain behind scrubbed references and bounded retention.
items.statement: Panel state, session rows and command blocks are explicitly historical GUI/evidence state; runtime must revalidate process identity and stored command or transcript content is ref-only and scrubbed.
items.title: Terminal session and command replay has a clear non-authority boundary

items.impact: Running sessions or commands may carry exit codes and finish times, terminal outcomes may omit them, timestamps may reverse, and active-process refs may contradict closed or restore-required state, producing misleading GUI and recovery behavior.
items.statement: TerminalSessionRecord and TerminalCommandBlock enumerate states but do not condition exit_code, finished_at_utc, process_identity_ref or transcript_ref on those states and do not enforce timestamp ordering.
items.title: Terminal lifecycle rows permit contradictory status evidence

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Deferred GUI projections restore panel/browser/preview state without launch authority.",
"replay_behavior": "Recovery resume uses checkpoint marker events plus safe-point/restore records; projector checkpoints alone are insufficient.",

items.impact: Tooling, GitHub/browser, goal, analytics, configuration and permission/recovery inventories cannot be treated as executable schemas, and recovery cannot rely on a disposable projector checkpoint alone.
items.statement: The remaining grouped inventories are consistently deferred with owners and reopen conditions; GUI projections lack launch authority, canonical goal events and receipts outrank projections, and permission recovery requires checkpoint markers plus safe-point or restore records.
items.title: Deferred GUI, analytics and recovery families retain explicit authority seams

segments.summary: Reviewed registry identity and scope plus ApprovedPlanPack and approval-outbox contracts; confirmed fail-closed authority boundaries and found collection, hash and status-correlation gaps.
Reviewed PlanCompileRun and CompilerWaveContract; confirmed runtime-disabled replay and found opaque lifecycle state plus unenforced wave isolation and receipt invariants.
Reviewed WorkGraphDraft and WorkNodeRequest; confirmed non-executable status and found missing graph-semantic and intake-completeness enforcement.
Reviewed ExecutorIntakeReport and AttemptReceipt; confirmed explanatory replay boundaries and found opaque outcome objects and missing status-dependent evidence rules.
Reviewed EventRecordIndex and BlockedProjection; confirmed authoritative-seglog and rebuildable-projection boundaries and found hash-shape and projection-safety matrix gaps.
Reviewed GoalReceipt and legacy/later inventories; confirmed projection and defer/reopen boundaries and found an unenforced goal-certification oracle.
Reviewed deferred projection groups and materialized terminal layout families; confirmed historical GUI truth and found pane-tree, ordering, selection, localization and accessibility gaps.
Reviewed terminal panel/session/command schemas and remaining deferred surface families; confirmed non-authority and recovery seams and found terminal status-evidence contradictions.

cross_document_questions: Which owner documents define the internal schemas for PlanCompile cursor/currentness/cancellation/supersession and the seven Executor intake domain-result objects?
Where are state-dependent certification rules that prohibit accepted GoalReceipt or Executor intake outcomes without positive validator and evidence refs?
Which terminal owner contract defines pane-tree acyclicity, selection referential integrity, lifecycle field matrices, accessible naming and localization behavior?
research_queries: JSON Schema 2020-12 conditional state machine invariants for receipts and outbox rows
JSON Schema graph referential integrity and acyclicity validation limitations
durable terminal session history redaction retention and process-liveness revalidation patterns
